cells.tense: You are standing in the yield now, and you are weighing it honestly.
cells.ask: Name one thing worth keeping from this year, then hand it to someone who would actually use it.
cells.core:
You're standing in the yield now, and you're weighing it honestly. You wait well, and you can take what that waiting grew and get it onto the table. Nothing here gets rounded up. You can look at a season and say what it actually produced, including the parts that came in small.

What steers this is the pull you already checked against. It shows you what deserves a place, and just as useful, what doesn't — and you don't keep the second kind out of habit or pass it off as treasure. That's the line between what's really yours and what you picked up because it was bright.

When you set it down and the account is plainly yours, that reading holds. You looked, you chose, and what's on the table is what you meant to bring.
cells.sheetLine: You waited, you looked, and you're keeping what's yours.
cells.verb: taking stock of what came through and deciding what is worth keeping

cells.tense: You are counting the yield before it has come in, and the counting is running the day.
cells.ask: Cut one thing from the plan that hasn't happened yet and leave the space empty today.
cells.core:
You're bracing for a harvest still in the ground. The pull toward what's ahead is strong, and underneath it you're already counting what it should produce — touching the return before it's handed over, running the review before the work is done.

That changes the pull itself. It stops being a draw and becomes a performance review. Fields don't ripen because someone measures them, and something that wanted to be lived quietly now has to produce for you first or it's failing. You're writing in the returns before they've accrued.

No number arrives halfway. Let what you're moving toward move at its own speed, and the pull stays a pull.

cells.tense: You were still standing at the door when it had already opened behind you.
cells.ask: Feed the one thing you still enjoy; do that one thing this week and let it be enough.
cells.core:
You're not taking stock of what came through, and there's plenty to take. Something's already grown and sitting in your hands, and you don't count it. Look at it plainly and you can feel that it used to have a pull. Done well, this is a small move: you name what draws you and set the day against it, plain answer, no performance.

What you want doesn't get named. There's a way of knowing quietly and not saying it, so the aim stays vague, and then there's nothing to check the days against. Nothing is being measured against it right now.

Start with the small thing that still has feeling in it. The pull comes back by use, not by waiting.

cells.tense: What you are steering is already running, yet you describe it as luck.
cells.ask: Say plainly, to one person, what you actually decided and why — the words you've been leaving out.
cells.core:
You already took stock. You decided — you can hear your own leaning whenever the topic surfaces — and you keep handing the credit somewhere else. A pull that should have your name on it gets called the timing, the momentum, or just how it went.

Except it isn't that. You notice what you notice and you gather where you gather. Because none of it gets said, the steering reads as drift. You set the value and acted on it, turn after turn; the shape is yours.

The gap now is only about saying so. Your call and your language are the same act. Put the claim in the room, where the whole thing can hold.

attempts.check: The draft's one unsupported claim is likely to be that 'collecting gives you solid proof something meaningful happened' — the record shows the gathering is happening but never says it eases present feeling, so that causal line is the reader's to disown. Second: Too Little is narrowed to harvest 'slipping past unfelt,' but the record's Too Little is past-anchored, so a reader could fairly say the miss belongs to something further back; the cell keeps today in view and lets that objection stand. The ask survives a wrong read because it only asks for the heat of something today to be written down, not for why it was kept, and if the read is wrong they still have the record-line. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person: 'the gathering is rarely wasted' — it flatters the keeping instead of showing the tail it's spending.
